## Root cause

`typescript` — the package that provides the `tsc` binary — lives in `devDependencies`, which is normal since it's a build-time-only tool. But the Dockerfile does this, in this order:

```
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
RUN npm run build
```

`npm ci --omit=dev` installs `node_modules` *without* devDependencies **before** the build ever runs. So when `npm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`) executes, it's running in an environment where the compiler's own toolchain is incomplete — the full TypeScript compilation of the entrypoint never happens, so `dist/server.js` never gets written. The one thing that does land in `dist/` is `dist/types/`, because that piece of output doesn't depend on whatever got stripped by `--omit=dev` — so `npm run build` still exits `0` (the RUN step "succeeds") even though it produced an incomplete `dist/`.

Locally, `npm run build` works because you're running it against a normal `npm install`, which keeps devDependencies intact — so `tsc` has everything it needs and emits the full `dist/`, including `dist/server.js`.

At runtime, `node dist/server.js` (from `"start": "node dist/server.js"`) fails immediately with:

```
Error: Cannot find module '/app/dist/server.js'
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1145:15)
```

because that file was never produced in the image.

## The fix

Install full dependencies (including dev) before building, then prune dev dependencies afterward, right before the runtime stage/`CMD`:

```
RUN npm ci
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --omit=dev
```

The key change is simply removing `--omit=dev` from the install step that precedes `npm run build`, so `tsc` and everything else `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` needs is present when the build actually runs. `npm prune --omit=dev` (run *after* the build) then gets you back to a lean production `node_modules` for runtime, without starving the build step.

The more robust, production-grade version of the same fix is a multi-stage Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
FROM node:20 AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json .
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json .
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
```

This way the `builder` stage always has devDependencies for `tsc`, and the final runtime image only ever gets the compiled `dist/` plus a lean `--omit=dev` `node_modules`, so `dist/server.js` is guaranteed to exist when `node dist/server.js` runs.
